summary.oneLiner: Neelamalai Agro Industries is a South Indian tea plantation company that cultivates, manufactures, sells and exports 100% Orthodox tea from its Katary and Sutton estates in the Nilgiris.
summary.business: The Company is engaged in Plantation activity, with tea as the crop dealt with; the main business is tea cultivation, tea manufacturing, and the sale and export of tea. It operates the Katary and Sutton Estates in the Nilgiris District of Tamil Nadu, spanning 631.769 hectares, with a factory that has facilities to produce Orthodox Tea. Currently the company produces 100% Orthodox Tea, and tea production during the year included bought leaf alongside its own estate crop.

risks.risk: Cost of production rising faster than sale realisation
risks.note: Management calls this the major threat for the plantation industry - the yearly increase in cost of production is not at all proportionate with the increase in sale realization, which structurally compresses plantation margins.
Plantation crops are generally prone to vagaries of nature and erratic monsoon, so crop volume and quality are outside management control.
Market potential exists for tea but is constrained by stiff competition from global, national and local players, limiting pricing power.
Any recession in the general economy may affect the plantation industry also; the outlook depends on consistent demand for plantation crops throughout the year.

The Company is engaged only in plantation activity, the crop dealt with is Tea, and it currently produces 100% Orthodox Tea from two estates in the Nilgiris District - so earnings depend on one crop, one product form and one growing region.

risks.risk: Realisation dependence on Orthodox tea prices and the packet tea segment
risks.note: The outlook is stated to depend on a higher realization commensurate with the cost of production and on the growth of the packet tea segment; the sale price for Orthodox Tea increased over the previous year, making earnings sensitive to that price cycle.
Credit risk on exports is identified by management and is mitigated by insuring the credit through Export Credit and Guarantee Corporation Limited (ECGC).

risks.risk: Asset and financial risk on fixed and current assets
risks.note: Managed through adequate insurance coverage of fixed and current assets and a conservative debt policy under which the debt component is very marginal.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Neelamalai Agro Industries is a South Indian tea plantation company that cultivates, manufactures, sells and exports 100% Orthodox tea from its Katary and Sutton estates in the Nilgiris.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is engaged in Plantation activity, with tea as the crop dealt with; the main business is tea cultivation, tea manufacturing, and the sale and export of tea. It operates the Katary and Sutton Estates in the Nilgiris District of Tamil Nadu, spanning 631.769 hectares, with a factory that has facilities to produce Orthodox Tea. Currently the company produces 100% Orthodox Tea, and tea production during the year included bought leaf alongside its own estate crop.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:

- AVT Natural Products Ltd — associate: Listed under Form AOC-1 Part B as an associate/joint venture; also a related party under common control through constitution of Board / shareholding, with ongoing sales of tea / tea waste at market rate. Several directors of the Company also sit on its board.
- A. V. Thomas & Co. Ltd. — related party: Common control through constitution of Board / shareholding; ongoing transactions covering sale of tea, rent and SAP expenses, all at market rate and on an arm's-length basis.

- Mr. Siddharth Thomas — related party: Relative of Promoter; ongoing consultancy-fee arrangement at market rate.
- Saksoft Limited — related party: Not a subsidiary/associate of the Company; disclosed as another listed entity where Mr. Ajit Thomas is a Non-Executive Non-Independent Director and Mrs. Kavitha Vijay is a Non-Executive Independent Director.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Industry outlook depends on consistent demand for Plantation Crops throughout the year
- Industry outlook depends on a higher realization commensurate with the cost of production
- Industry outlook depends on the growth of the packet tea segment
- Sale price for Orthodox Tea has increased compared with the previous year
- Market potential exists for tea, but is constrained by stiff competition from global, national and local players
- Yearly increase in cost of production is not proportionate with the increase in sale realization
- Plantation crops are prone to vagaries of nature and erratic monsoon; a general economic recession may affect the plantation industry

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Quality upgradation and attainment of cost efficiency are stated as the prime missions of the Company
- Plant modernization and field development undertaken in support of the quality and cost-efficiency missions
- Continuous upgradation of Human Resources, with training programmes for employees at all levels, to improve productivity and quality of produce
- Maintain a minimal-risk business strategy, including a conservative debt policy and adequate insurance coverage of fixed and current assets
- Periodic upgradation and review of information systems resources
- The sections provided articulate no formal dividend, buyback or reinvestment policy. The only capital-allocation intent disclosed is procedural: the Notice of the 83rd Annual General Meeting (to be held on 19th August 2026 through VC/OAVM) places the declaration of dividend on equity shares before members as ordinary business. The Board's stated role includes setting the annual business plan and considering proposals for diversification, investments and business re-organisation. Form AOC-1 records no subsidiaries (Part A - NIL) and no associate or joint venture liquidated, sold, or yet to commence operations during the year, indicating a stable holding structure rather than active portfolio churn.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no rupee capex plan, no capacity addition and no dated expansion project. The Company's asset footprint is its two tea estates in the Nilgiris District of Tamil Nadu - Katary Estate (Katary Post, Coonoor) and Sutton Estate (Kullakamby Post) - together spanning 631.769 Hectares, with a factory that has facilities to produce Orthodox Tea and currently produces 100% Orthodox Tea. The only forward-looking investment language is qualitative: plant modernization and field development have been undertaken with the missions of quality upgradation and cost efficiency in mind, and the Company has upgraded all its information systems resources with periodic review. No commissioning, ramp-up, debottlenecking, new site, acquisition or JV adding capacity or geography is disclosed in the sections provided.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Owned estate base of 631.769 hectares across Katary and Sutton Estates in the Nilgiris, giving backward integration into leaf
- 100% Orthodox Tea production with good manufacturing practices and HACCP systems followed in the tea factory
- Conservative debt policy with a very marginal debt component
- Adequate insurance coverage of fixed and current assets, and export credit insured through ECGC
- Internal control framework with a leading firm of Chartered Accountants appointed as Internal Auditors
- Employee strength of 810 as on 31st March 2026, with training programmes organised for employees at all levels

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Cost of production rising faster than sale realisation — Management calls this the major threat for the plantation industry - the yearly increase in cost of production is not at all proportionate with the increase in sale realization, which structurally compresses plantation margins.
- Weather dependence and erratic monsoon — Plantation crops are generally prone to vagaries of nature and erratic monsoon, so crop volume and quality are outside management control.
- Competitive intensity in tea — Market potential exists for tea but is constrained by stiff competition from global, national and local players, limiting pricing power.
- Macroeconomic / demand cyclicality — Any recession in the general economy may affect the plantation industry also; the outlook depends on consistent demand for plantation crops throughout the year.
- Single-crop, single-activity concentration — The Company is engaged only in plantation activity, the crop dealt with is Tea, and it currently produces 100% Orthodox Tea from two estates in the Nilgiris District - so earnings depend on one crop, one product form and one growing region.
- Realisation dependence on Orthodox tea prices and the packet tea segment — The outlook is stated to depend on a higher realization commensurate with the cost of production and on the growth of the packet tea segment; the sale price for Orthodox Tea increased over the previous year, making earnings sensitive to that price cycle.
- Export credit risk — Credit risk on exports is identified by management and is mitigated by insuring the credit through Export Credit and Guarantee Corporation Limited (ECGC).
- Asset and financial risk on fixed and current assets — Managed through adequate insurance coverage of fixed and current assets and a conservative debt policy under which the debt component is very marginal.
